key_insight: Realistic piezoelectric surface deformations can generate wall waves that significantly alter near-wall turbulence, with spanwise waves delivering the strongest drag reduction.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to passive/active hybrid drag-control surfaces for reducing skin-friction in turbulent channels and potentially improving fluid-transport efficiency.
method: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent half-channel flow at Re_tau=200.
Finite-element analysis of piezoelectric actuation beneath an aluminum sheet over 119–543 Hz and 250–500 V.
Applied resulting wall deformations as bottom-wall boundary conditions to test upstream, downstream, and spanwise wave effects.
evidence_signal: The study reports maximum drag reductions of 1.6% for upstream waves, 5.4% for downstream waves, and 27.6% for spanwise waves, with the strongest effect from the realistic spanwise hybrid wave.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated at Re_tau=200 in DNS, so robustness, durability, and scalability to higher-Reynolds-number real flows and hardware constraints remain to be validated.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent drag reduction via piezoelectric actuation
